lesson.menu_desc: Reading and comparing two partnership offers, and saying which one is better and why -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Two Proposals
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Juliana dos Santos Morais | Lesson 6 -- Two Proposals
lesson.grammar_point: comparatives, superlatives and not as ... as for comparing proposals

listenings.text: I choose sponsors for five or six events every year, and I always ask three questions. First: is this company a good fit for our members? A sponsor has to be interesting for the people in the room. Second: what does the sponsor want in return? The biggest offer is not always the best one, because some sponsors ask for too much. For example, a long presentation in the middle of a breakfast. And third: is the company reliable? In my experience, a reliable sponsor that pays on time is more valuable than a famous sponsor that pays three months late. So I do not only compare the numbers. I compare the whole package.

A few years ago, our company sponsored big international conferences. They were famous, and we had a lot of visibility. But they were also very expensive, and honestly, not very effective. We met hundreds of people, but very few of them became partners. Now we sponsor smaller events at a chamber of commerce. The package is more affordable, and the events are much more cost-effective for us. The best benefit is direct contact with the people who make decisions in the member companies. It is not as glamorous as a big conference, but the results are better.

paras: Every year, the chamber organizes a business breakfast for its member companies, and every year it needs a sponsor. This year, two companies sent a proposal. The first is a large Canadian bank. The second is a Brazilian logistics company that joined the chamber two years ago.

The bank offers the bigger amount of money: it can pay seventy percent of the budget. It is also the most famous name, so it brings more visibility to the event. But its proposal has a drawback. The bank wants a long presentation during the breakfast, and many members think these presentations are the least interesting part of the event.

The logistics company offers less money, but its package is more flexible. It does not ask for a presentation, and it offers to transport all the materials for free. It is also more reliable in one important way: it has sponsored three events with the chamber before, and it has always paid on time. So the decision is not simple. The bank is not as flexible as the logistics company, but it is the most generous. The organizers have to decide what is more important for the members this year.
